title: Stroke in the hospital: ischemic, hemorrhage or TIA
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the cerebrovascular event (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/14/2026

Reason for Admission:
Evaluation for transient ischemic attack.

HPI:
[Copied Forward] Patient is a 55-year-old male who presented to the emergency department following a sudden onset of sensory and motor deficits in the right upper extremity. Symptoms were reported to have resolved spontaneously within one hour. The patient denies any preceding headache, dizziness, or vision changes. He denies any history of similar episodes.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted for a transient ischemic attack to undergo neurological workup and risk factor modification. A non-contrast head MRI was performed, which demonstrated no evidence of acute brain injury or permanent tissue damage. Neurological examinations were performed repeatedly during the admission period, with all findings remaining within normal limits. Laboratory work showed no evidence of metabolic derangements. The patient was started on an aspirin regimen and counseled on blood pressure management and lifestyle modifications to reduce the risk of future neurological events. He was stable for discharge.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, or fatigue.
Neurological: Positive for transient ischemic attack (resolved). Negative for seizures or tremors.
Cardiovascular: Negative for palpitations or chest pain.
Respiratory: Negative for shortness of breath or cough.
Gastrointestinal: Negative for nausea or diarrhea.
Musculoskeletal: Negative for joint pain or swelling.

Social History:
Lives with spouse and two children. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol consumption. Works as a project manager.

Family History:
Father had hypertension and hypertension-related complications. Mother had type 2 diabetes.

Vitals:
BP: 128/82, HR: 74, SpO2: 98% on room air, Temp: 98.6 F.

Recent Labs:
Sodium: 139 mEq/L, Potassium: 4.2 mEq/L, Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL, Glucose: 105 mg/dL, WBC: 7.5 x 10^3/uL.

Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Transient ischemic attack
2. Hypertension

Discharge Medications:
1. Aspirin 81 mg daily
2. Lisinopril 10 mg daily

Follow-up:
Follow up with primary care physician in 1 week for blood pressure monitoring and continued risk factor management.

Electronically signed, J. Lindqvist, MD, 05/14/2026
explanations: Transient ischemic attack: G45.9 (no HCC). There is no infarction, so it is not a stroke.

distractors.why: Symptoms resolved and MRI shows no infarction: TIA, not stroke.
